items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: And Tizol, Juan Tizol, we were very friendly with him, and Sonny. Of course everybody that's met Sonny is his friend right off the bat.

ctx.x: I see. And you said it was Irving Mills didn't feel they could spare a horn player to play

Well, he wanted more of a Latin sound than they were getting there, and of course Sonny was the only percussionist there at the moment, and so he suggested that I play the maracas, and that's how I happened to -- I happened to be in the studio.

I see. Back to you and your music. When did you get started? I read in one of the many, many books I've been reading about you that your uncle gave you a saxophone when you were eight years old. Is that correct?
